expectedText:
EXEMPT / NON-EXEMPT CLASSIFICATION NOTICE
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

THE DEFAULT RULE
Federal law generally requires Acme, Inc. to pay Jordan Lee at least one and one-half times the regular rate of pay for hours worked beyond 40 in a workweek. This overtime requirement applies unless Jordan Lee's position qualifies for a specific exemption under federal law — classifying a position as exempt isn't a label a company can apply by choice; it depends on meeting the actual legal test below.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "Except as otherwise provided in this section, no employer shall employ any of his employees who in any workweek is engaged in commerce or in the production of goods for commerce ... for a workweek longer than forty hours unless such employee receives compensation for his employment in excess of the hours above specified at a rate not less than one and one-half times the regular rate at which he is employed."
  — 29 U.S.C. § 207(a)(1) (Cornell LII text), U.S. Code (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/207)
  "The general overtime pay standard in section 7(a) requires that overtime must be compensated at a rate not less than one and one-half times the regular rate at which the employee is actually employed."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 778.107 (Cornell LII text), Electronic Code of Federal Regulations, DOL's own restatement of the overtime rate (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/778.107)
  Known gap: This describes the federal floor only. Some states set a higher overtime threshold, a daily overtime requirement in addition to the weekly one, or a higher minimum salary for exemption than federal law requires — this document doesn't catalog those stricter state rules.

THE EXEMPTION TEST
To qualify as exempt under the most commonly used federal exemptions — executive, administrative, and professional — a position generally must meet three conditions: the employee must be paid on a salary basis rather than by the hour; that salary must meet a minimum weekly amount set by federal regulation; and the employee's actual job duties, not their job title, must satisfy a specific duties test for the exemption being claimed. For the executive exemption specifically, that duties test requires the employee's primary duty to be managing the business or a recognized department, regularly directing the work of at least two other employees, and having real authority — or a real say — in hiring, firing, or similar personnel decisions.

[Verified — checked 2026-08-30]
  "any employee employed in a bona fide executive, administrative, or professional capacity (including any employee employed in the capacity of academic administrative personnel or teacher in elementary or secondary schools), or in the capacity of outside salesman"
  — 29 U.S.C. § 213(a)(1) (Cornell LII text), U.S. Code, Fair Labor Standards Act, white-collar exemptions (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/213)
  "The term “employee employed in a bona fide executive capacity” in section 13(a)(1) of the Act shall mean any employee: (1) Compensated on a salary basis pursuant to § 541.600 at a rate of not less than $684 per week ... exclusive of board, lodging or other facilities; (2) Whose primary duty is management of the enterprise in which the employee is employed or of a customarily recognized department or subdivision thereof; (3) Who customarily and regularly directs the work of two or more other employees; and (4) Who has the authority to hire or fire other employees or whose suggestions and recommendations as to the hiring, firing, advancement, promotion or any other change of status of other employees are given particular weight."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 541.100 (Cornell LII text), Code of Federal Regulations, general rule for executive employees (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/541.100)
  "To qualify as an exempt executive, administrative or professional employee under section 13(a)(1) of the Act, an employee must be compensated on a salary basis at a rate of not less than $684 per week ... exclusive of board, lodging or other facilities."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 541.600 (Cornell LII text), Code of Federal Regulations, amount of salary required (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/541.600)
  Known gap: The administrative, professional, computer, and outside-sales exemptions each have their own separate duties test under this same set of regulations — this clause describes the executive exemption's test as one concrete example, not all five. Meeting the salary requirements alone never qualifies a position as exempt without also satisfying the duties test for whichever exemption is actually being claimed, and satisfying a duties test alone doesn't qualify a position that isn't also paid on a salary basis at or above the minimum amount.

CLASSIFICATION
Position: Software Engineer

Classification: ☐ Exempt  ☐ Non-Exempt

If exempt, exemption claimed (e.g., executive, administrative, professional): _______________________________________________
Salary (if exempt) or hourly rate (if non-exempt): _______________

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to acknowledge this classification.

Employee: Jordan Lee
Date: _______________

—
